rule: Tickets are sold in the online ticket shop (ksc.de/tickets, tickets.ksc.de), from the day after the online start also in the FanWelt at the BBBank Wildpark and the Fanshop am Rondellplatz, and on matchday at the stadium box offices when tickets remain. Buying online needs a KSC-ID, a free registration with name, e-mail, address and date of birth; one e-mail address per KSC-ID.

Membership is not required for an ordinary home game, which reaches free sale. A passive adult membership (Klassik, 18+) costs EUR 75 a year from 1 Jul 2026 (EUR 70 reduced, EUR 90 Premium); 7-17 year-olds pay EUR 40; 0-6 year-olds are free but get no presale right. Membership starts once the application is processed and confirmed by e-mail, which currently takes up to 30 working days; the member's KSC-ID is then unlocked for members' presales.
note: ONE SOURCE, the club's own membership page; no second source for the fee was found. The club plans EUR 90 for every adult from July 2027 (EUR 80 with Supporters Karlsruhe membership). For the derby a membership is the practical route in (see free-sale-reached): two people need two memberships, since a KSC-ID carries one presale right. The processing time matters: an application made only when the sale is announced may not be processed in time.

rule: One presale right per KSC-ID: buying several season tickets on one KSC-ID still gives one right. Children's (0-6) and corporate memberships carry none.

rule: The club's own Ticketzweitmarkt is the only legal platform for reselling and buying KSC home tickets. rule: The ticket terms forbid offering tickets on unauthorised platforms (named: viagogo, StubHub, Ticketbande, Gigsberg, eBay, eBay Kleinanzeigen, Facebook, seatwave) even without profit, and passing a ticket on above the original price; a mark-up of up to 15% for transaction costs is allowed. Tickets offered on unauthorised platforms can be cancelled without compensation.
note: ATGB 10.2. A private handover (illness, being prevented) is allowed under ATGB 10.3 through the Zweitmarkt or with the club told who the new holder is. The Landgericht Mannheim prohibited viagogo from selling unauthorised KSC tickets (K34, a legal blog's account, Jan 2026).

The buyer must carry an official photo ID and show it on request; entry can be refused when holder and registered buyer differ outside a permitted handover. On suspicion the club may ask for a copy of the buyer's ID before confirming an order.
note: ATGB 2.4, 2.7 and 11.2 d. One source - the club's terms; no report of ID checks at the gate was read.

rule: A ticket may be passed on privately for non-commercial reasons, for example illness: through the club's Zweitmarkt, or directly if the new holder accepts the terms and the club is told, on request, the new holder's name, address and date of birth. Passing a home-area ticket to a fan of the visiting club is forbidden.
note: ATGB 9.3 f and 9.4. The help centre words it more loosely: day tickets may be passed on among friends at the original price (V8).

rule: The club's own Ticketbörse is the only legal resale route. Day tickets can be listed only for sold-out games, from one week before; season-ticket seats from two weeks before. The ticket is blocked and re-released; other fans buy it at the official price through the regular sale, and the seller is refunded the price minus a 20% handling fee.
note: The Ticketbörse for day tickets is new from 2025-26 (V1). The ATGB say only that the seller is credited the original price less costs (V11). DOES NOT SIT EASILY WITH GERMANY'S DFL ROW (country-ticket-rules.csv, resale-price-cap): the DFL's fair-play rules cap the service fee for the official secondary market at 15% of the order value, and VfB keeps 20% from the seller. Either VfB is not one of the clubs in the DFL scheme (the DFL page does not say every club takes part), or the 15% means a buyer-side fee. Not settled; nothing changed on either side.

rule: Offering a ticket at auctions, on unauthorised platforms (named: eBay, eBay Kleinanzeigen, seatwave, viagogo, StubHub, ticketbande, ticketbis) or on social media is forbidden, as is any commercial resale. A private handover may not exceed the original price by more than 20% plus a EUR 5 transaction fee. Tickets offered on unauthorised platforms give no right of entry, and the club pursues sellers with contractual penalties.
note: THE CLUB'S OWN PAGES DISAGREE ON THE CAP: the terms (V11 9.3 d) allow +20% plus EUR 5; the help centre (V8) says day tickets may be passed on 'zum Originalpreis'. Both are written; the terms are the contract. Germany's DFL row caps the official secondary market at the original price - VfB's Ticketbörse is its implementation.

rule: Sale dates for each game are announced in the ticket shop's event calendar and by e-mail; the club's news section carries ticket articles and visitor information per game.
note: This is what the updateTracking cell of club-tickets.csv rests on. No notify button was found.

rule: Children under 14 are admitted only with an adult who also holds a ticket; children under 7 are not admitted to standing areas. Reduced prices apply to under-18s (proof of age required unasked when buying) and a child price to children up to 13 in some areas. Under-18s can join the Fritzle-Club (5-12, applied for with the parents) or the Jugendclub (13-18), both with a presale right after three months. The REWE family block (blocks 75, 76, 81, 82) is sold only to Fritzle- and Jugendclub members, from EUR 20 per person for the parent-and-child ticket.
note: WHAT IS NOT STATED: whether a person under 18 may buy in their own account. Under-18s can also be e.V. members (EUR 21 up to 14, EUR 30 from 15, V5) - so the hand-written note that an under-18 joins the kids' clubs 'not the adult e.V.' is not quite what the fee table says.

rule: VfB's tickets for an away game go first to away-season-ticket holders and to the official fan clubs (allocated by the fan liaison), then to members through a sale or, where the members' share is under 500, an application with a draw; with a small allocation there is no members' sale at all. A non-member gets no ticket from VfB's allocation.
note: The last sentence is a reading of the rule, not a sentence the club wrote: every phase named is for holders, fan clubs or members.

rule: For a non-member the realistic routes to an away game are the home club's own sale, outside VfB's allocation - for example Hoffenheim's free sale for the September 2026 game, about 3,000 tickets, max two per person - with the home club's rules on visiting fans in home areas.
note: A SYNTHESIS from one case (V29, paywalled, readable part only). Whether a given home club sells to non-members, and where, is that club's rule.

rule: For a non-member the realistic routes to a home game are: a free sale when the members' sale leaves tickets (every Bundesliga home game of early 2026, none known so far in 2026-27); or a membership taken out well ahead - about two weeks' processing plus three months before the presale right works - which then covers two tickets. Top games and Champions League games have sold out in the members' sale. The Ticketbörse resells returns for sold-out games, but appears to be visible to members.
note: A SYNTHESIS, not a club statement. FOR A TOP GAME IN 2026-27: the Bayern home game is a placeholder at late January 2027; by the six-weeks pattern its members' sale would open in December 2026, and a membership started in October 2026 would get its presale right only around mid-January 2027 - probably too late for that game.

rule: Free sale was held for the Frankfurt and Union Berlin home games of January 2026 after the members' sale left adjacent seats, mainly at the side of the Gegengerade near the guest area. By 10 Mar 2026 every Bundesliga home game of 2026 had had a free sale. The Bayern home game of December 2025 was sold out, with returns only through the Zweitmarkt.
note: V19 and V20 are one newsroom (Stuttgarter Nachrichten / Stuttgarter Zeitung), so the free-sale facts rest on one press source plus the club's own sale list being public.

rule: No free sale for a 2026-27 home game was found. On 7 Oct 2026 the club's shop showed the Atlético (Champions League) and Gladbach games sold out in the members' sale, with a release of remaining places 'possible'.
note: ONE SOURCE, a live page. 'Possible' release is not a free sale.

rule: Fans in the visiting club's kit are not admitted to the Cannstatter Kurve, the home standing area (blocks 31-50), which the club marks as an active atmosphere area with standing and flags.
note: The kit rule is stated in the 2025-26 Bayern visitor information (V23); the standing-area designation in V1 and V12. How the guest area itself is sold was not read.

rule: The sources give different figures for the MHPArena: 60,058 (German Wikipedia's infobox, on the map, and the 2026-27 attendance for the Köln game), 60,449 (the 2011 figure, and English Wikipedia's highest 2025-26 home attendance), 54,812 all-seated for international games - while English Wikipedia gives 57,000-60,000 for Champions League and Europa League home games.
note: A GAP. No club figure was read. A 2025-26 attendance of 60,449 is above the 60,058 now given as capacity; European attendances are above 54,812. None is reconciled.

rule: No credible data on actual secondary-market prices for VfB home games.
note: A GAP, so club-ticket-prices.csv has no resale-observed row. Resellers' asking prices were seen in search results (StubHub, Hellotickets and others); an asking price on a platform the club bans is not a price paid.
